title: DCGI Alerts States After Misbranded Abhayrab Rabies Vaccine Batch Fails Potency Test

contentHtml:
New Delhi: Drug regulatory and law enforcement agencies have intensified coordinated action against the illegal manufacture, distribution and supply of misbranded and spurious drugs following the seizure of a purported batch of the rabies vaccine Abhayrab from an unlicensed premises in Delhi.

According to a public notice issued on September 5, 2026, the product, bearing Batch No. KE25012, was subsequently found to be misbranded and not manufactured by Indian Immunologicals Limited.

The Crime Branch of Delhi Police has been maintaining continuous surveillance to identify criminal activities relating to the manufacture and distribution of misbranded and spurious drugs. The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) works in close coordination with Delhi Police and other enforcement agencies whenever leads concerning such criminal activities emerge.

As part of the continuing surveillance and enforcement exercise, on April 22, 2026, the Crime Branch, Delhi Police, along with a team of Drugs Inspectors from the Drugs Control Department, Government of NCT of Delhi, conducted a search at an unlicensed premises situated at Flat No. 20/7, Indra Vikas, Second Floor, Mukherjee Nagar, Delhi–110009. During the search, Rabies Vaccine (Abhayrab), bearing Batch No. KE25012, was seized from the premises.

CDSCO officials were called to the premises for legal sampling of the seized vaccine. The samples were forwarded to the Central Drugs Laboratory (CDL), Kasauli, the government vaccine-testing laboratory, for examination. Following laboratory examination, the product was reported as misbranded and Not of Standard Quality.

According to the attached Certificate of Test or Analysis in Form 13, the sample was received from Mr P. Selvaraj, Drugs Inspector, CDSCO, North Zone, CGO Building-I, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, Kamla Nehru Nagar, Hapur Chungi, Ghaziabad–201002, Uttar Pradesh. The Drugs Inspector’s memorandum was identified as NZ/SMP/PS-A/013/2026/466-67, dated April 23, 2026. The laboratory received 30 vials of 0.5 mL each on May 11, 2026.

The product purported to be Rabies Vaccine Human, IP (Purified Vero Cell Rabies Vaccine), under the brand name Abhayrab. The vaccine details mentioned Batch No. KE25012, CDL No. 2932/2026, manufacturing date August 2025 and expiry date July 2028. The accompanying diluent bore Batch No. IVK5010, manufacturing date May 2025 and expiry date April 2029.

The product label instructed that the vaccine should be stored at 2°C to 8°C and should not be frozen. However, the certificate recorded that the sample had been stored at room temperature while being collected. The product was labelled as manufactured in India by Human Biologicals Institute, a division of Indian Immunologicals Limited, Survey Nos. 281–284 and 321, Biotech Park, Phase-III, Karkapatla Village, Markook Mandal, Siddipet District–502281, Telangana, India.

The pack size was described as one shrink-wrapped pack containing 15 cartons, with each carton containing a 0.5 mL vial and a 0.5 mL Water for Injection ampoule. The condition of the seals on the packet, sample portion or container was found to be intact and comparable with the specimen seal.

In the opinion of the Government Analyst, the sample was Not of Standard Quality and a misbranded drug under Section 17 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Rules made thereunder in respect of the tests mentioned in the report. The laboratory also advised that further investigation may be carried out to verify the applicability of Section 17B concerning spurious drugs under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Rules made thereunder.

The sample complied with the physical-aspects test and passed the sterility, moisture-content, thiomersal and identity tests. However, the sample failed the potency test, while its label review was also found not to comply.

During the label review, CDL compared the sample submitted by the Drugs Inspector and received on May 11, 2026 with the retained sample of the same vaccine batch previously received from Human Biologicals Institute, Telangana, on September 30, 2025, under CDL No. 6293/2025, for lot-release testing. The retained sample had been released on November 7, 2025, through dispatch No. CDL/2025/8392.

The laboratory observed that the artwork of the Rabies Vaccine bearing Batch No. KE25012 submitted by the Drugs Inspector did not match the retained sample of the same batch. In the product name appearing after “Rabies Vaccine,” an apostrophe-like punctuation mark was present on the Drugs Inspector’s sample, whereas a comma was present on the retained sample.

The size and position of the registered trademark symbol appearing after the trade name Abhayrab were also different. The symbol was larger on the Drugs Inspector’s sample, while it was smaller and differently positioned on the retained sample. The spelling of “L. Pasteur” appeared as “L. Posteur” on the sample submitted by the Drugs Inspector.

The preservative concentration on the Drugs Inspector’s sample was represented as ≤0.015% w/w, whereas it appeared as ≤0.015% w/v on the retained sample. Similarly, the diluent concentration was represented as 0.9% w/w on the Drugs Inspector’s sample and as 0.9% w/v on the retained sample.

The text inside the warning box did not match, while the colour and style of the company’s logo were different. The artwork number on the Drugs Inspector’s sample was PLM0395/07/22, whereas the retained sample bore the artwork number PLM0395/08/24.

The QR code on the sample submitted by the Drugs Inspector could not be verified through GS1, while the QR code on the retained sample was verified by GS1. Differences were also observed in the text alignment. The diluent manufacturing licence number on the Drugs Inspector’s sample was mentioned as DD/449, whereas the retained sample carried the licence number 30/MD/AP/2013/F/G.

The font used for the batch-coding details—KE25012, 08/25, 07/28 and IVK5010, 05/25, 04/29—was different. The vial submitted by the Drugs Inspector had a blue cap, whereas the retained sample at CDL had a green cap. Other differences in fonts were also observed.

A hologram was pasted on the seal of the blue-capped vial submitted by the Drugs Inspector, whereas no hologram was pasted on the CDL-retained sample. The font and spacing alignment on the two vials were also different.

The annexure containing the visual comparison of the outer cartons further recorded that the font style and size on the Drugs Inspector’s sample differed from those on the retained sample. The words “For Sale in India Only” appeared in orange font on the sample submitted by the Drugs Inspector, whereas they appeared in red font on the retained sample at CDL.

The laboratory findings, including the specific particulars of the misbranding observed in the seized product, were communicated by the office of the Drugs Controller General (India) to the States and Union Territories for necessary regulatory vigilance and action.

Through a communication dated August 27, 2026, the DCGI requested all State Drugs Controllers to alert their inspectorate staff and maintain strict vigilance over the movement, distribution and availability of the specified batch of the drug. The State Drug Control authorities were also requested to take appropriate regulatory action, as considered necessary, under the provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Rules made thereunder. The communication sent to the States also enumerated the relevant details concerning the misbranding established through laboratory examination.

As a precautionary measure and to ensure that accurate information was available to the public, the manufacturer of Abhayrab also issued a public communication presenting the facts concerning the misbranded product. The manufacturer reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining the highest standards of quality in the manufacture and supply of its vaccines.

The manufacturer further stated that every batch of Abhayrab is released for sale only after independent testing and batch-release certification by CDL, Kasauli. Vaccines administered at hospitals, clinics and government healthcare facilities, or dispensed through licensed pharmacies, therefore reach patients through the authorised and regulated supply chain after undergoing the prescribed quality-control and batch-release procedures.

It was also confirmed that no part of the batch concerned had been exported to any other country.

The seizure and subsequent regulatory action form part of the continuing surveillance and enforcement mechanism of drug regulatory and law enforcement agencies to detect unauthorised manufacturing and distribution activities and prevent the circulation of misbranded and spurious medicines.

The public notice stated that the coordinated efforts of CDSCO, the State Drug Control authorities, the Drugs Control Department, GNCTD, and law enforcement agencies demonstrate the continuous vigilance and integrated enforcement mechanism in place to protect public health and ensure that medicines and vaccines available to the public meet the prescribed standards of quality and safety.

In connection with the case, four persons have been arrested by the Delhi Police. Further investigation and appropriate legal action are being undertaken by the competent authorities.
